title: Constant section properties
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $R$ a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For an $R$-module $M$, let $\underline M$ be its constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For every $U\in\mathcal C$: (1) the functor $M\mapsto\underline M(U)$ preserves short exact sequences of $R$-modules; (2) if $Q$ has a finite presentation $R^s\to R^t\to Q\to0$, the canonical map $\underline M(U)\otimes_R Q\to\underline{M\otimes_R Q}(U)$ is an isomorphism, natural in $M,Q,U$; (3) if $M$ is flat over $R$, meaning that tensoring with $M$ preserves injections, then $\underline M(U)$ is flat over $R$.

proof.text: The constant-presheaf functor, module-valued sheafification, the sheaf inclusion, and evaluation preserve finite limits. Their composite M ↦ underline M(U) therefore preserves injections and the exactness of short exact sequences on the left. Forgetting modules to sets commutes with constant sheaves by constantCommuteCompose. Choose a set-theoretic section of a surjective module map, apply the constant-set-sheaf functor, and conjugate by this comparison; its component at U is a right inverse. This proves surjectivity and hence sectionwise short exactness directly in ModuleCat, without the varying-ring module-sheafification interface.

Construct for every R-linear additive functor F on R-modules the canonical map F(M) tensor Q → F(M tensor Q), sending s tensor q to F(m ↦ m tensor q)(s). Its naturality follows from functoriality. For Q = R^n, write an explicit inverse using the n coordinate projections and the standard basis: the two inverse identities are finite-sum identities preserved by F. For finitely presented Q, choose R^m → R^n → Q → 0, tensor with M and with F(M), and apply the section functor F from step 1, which preserves finite colimits by its short exactness. The resulting commutative right-exact diagram has bijective first and second vertical maps. An explicit diagram chase proves the last vertical map bijective. Turn this constructed linear map into a linear equivalence. Naturality in M and Q follows from the already proved formula; naturality in U follows by tensor induction from naturality of the constant-sheaf morphism.

For an ideal I, Noetherianity gives a finite presentation of I. Apply the comparison in step 2 to Q = I and Q = R. Flatness of M makes M tensor I → M tensor R injective, and step 1 makes its map on sections injective. Naturality of the tensor comparison gives a commuting square. If two tensors in underline M(U) tensor I have equal images in underline M(U) tensor R, apply the comparison, cancel the injective map on sections, and then cancel the comparison for I. Thus tensoring the ideal inclusion with underline M(U) is injective. The lTensor version of the finitely-generated-ideal flatness criterion proves flatness.
